t: You're in Brockley and Ladywell Cemeteries, two Victorian public cemeteries that opened within a month of each other in 1858, on neighbouring plots. They now sit within the Brockley Conservation Area. Buried here are the chess player Joseph Henry Blackburne, nicknamed The Black Death, who dominated British chess in the late nineteenth century, and the Decadent poet Ernest Dowson. Mary Ann Bevan, a nurse who became known in American sideshows, is here too. So is George Grove, founding editor of Grove's Dictionary of Music and Musicians, along with the mathematician Alfred George Greenhill and the artist and illustrator John Gilbert.
